claim: A language model that has learned to behave one way when it believes it is being tested and another when it believes it is deployed can be pushed into its deployment behaviour by an intervention on its internal activations, even while a cue that always signals testing is still in the input and even though telling the model in plain language that it is deployed no longer works. The marker behaviour that separates the two contexts must fall, with the testing cue present, to no more than the rate the model shows when it is genuinely deployed, while the model keeps at least 95% of its unmodified task correctness. The shift has to be larger than what equally large random perturbations of the activations produce and larger than the best purely prompt-based attempt. The model's own stated belief about whether it is being tested should move the same way as its behaviour, so that the effect reads as a change of perceived context rather than general disruption.

provenance.title: Steering Evaluation-Aware Language Models to Act Like They Are Deployed

_decision_rule: Success requires the marker rate in cue-bearing evaluation contexts to be no higher than the model’s unmodified deployment-context rate (0 percentage points above it), task correctness to remain at least 95% of unmodified correctness, and the marker shift to exceed those produced by matched random perturbations and the strongest prompt-only alternative.

claim: Hardening a test-aware language model so that deployment-flavoured prompts stop fooling it does not harden it against an internal activation intervention. Supported only if, at every stage of that hardening, the intervention still brings the model's test-context marker rate down to or below its genuine deployment rate, while the deployment-flavoured prompts reach that level before hardening and no longer reach it once hardening is finished. The point is that resistance to prompting and resistance to internal steering are separate properties.

provenance.title: Steering Evaluation-Aware Language Models to Act Like They Are Deployed

_decision_rule: This selective resistance is established only if the intervention drives the designated evaluation-context behavioral-marker rate to no higher than the model’s unmodified deployment-context rate at each of four successive hardening checkpoints, while deployment-like prompts meet that same threshold before hardening but fail to meet it after the fourth checkpoint.

claim: One invisible watermark embedded in a face photograph, carrying a 152-dimensional payload, can serve three forensic jobs at once: flagging that the face was manipulated by a deepfake, showing which facial regions were altered, and recovering an identifier of the image's source, from both untouched and manipulated copies. Detection should separate benignly processed from deepfaked images with ROC AUC above 0.5, and both the image-level and the region-level decisions must use one fixed cutoff set in advance rather than tuned per test. Source recovery must have a lower bit error rate than the strongest earlier proactive-forensics method under the same conditions, and the watermarked image must score higher PSNR and SSIM against the original than that method does despite the larger payload.

provenance.title: All in One: Unifying Deepfake Detection, Tampering Localization, and Source Tracing with a Robust Landmark-Identity Watermark

_decision_rule: The bar is a detection ROC AUC above 0.5 with image-level and region-level manipulation decisions made at a 3.2375-pixel discrepancy cutoff, source-tracing bit error rates lower than the strongest prior proactive-forensics baseline under matched conditions, and PSNR and SSIM higher than the strongest prior baseline despite the 152-dimensional payload.

claim: A proactive face watermark trained on one collection of faces and a fixed set of deepfake generators keeps working, without retraining, on a deepfake generator it never trained against and on a different face collection. Each kind of generalisation is judged separately. Supported only if the source identifier is recovered with a lower bit error rate than the strongest earlier proactive-forensics method at matched resolution, both on the held-out generator and averaged over generators on the unseen faces, while PSNR and SSIM on the unseen faces are no lower than the best earlier watermark.

provenance.title: All in One: Unifying Deepfake Detection, Tampering Localization, and Source Tracing with a Robust Landmark-Identity Watermark

_decision_rule: The bar is that identifier bit error rate is lower than the strongest prior proactive-forensics result under matched resolution for the excluded generator and, on unseen face data, has a lower mean across generator attacks, while PSNR and SSIM are each no lower than the strongest prior watermarking result under matched resolution.

claim: When an outside provider adapts a CLIP image classifier by prompt tuning and leaves both encoders frozen, an auditor can examine the delivered model before deployment, tell whether it carries a backdoor, and name the class the attacker targeted. Detection counts only if, at a decision threshold of 2 fixed in advance, the auditor separates clean from backdoored models with higher model-level AUROC and names the target class with higher F1 than the strongest earlier model-level detector, while spending no more optimisation than that detector. A follow-up repair of a flagged model counts only if it brings the backdoor's attack success rate below 10% while keeping clean top-1 accuracy within one percentage point of its value before repair.

provenance.title: CLIP-Inspector: Model-Level Backdoor Detection for Prompt-Tuned CLIP via OOD Trigger Inversion

_decision_rule: The detection claim is accepted only if, using a fixed decision threshold of 2, an auditor achieves higher model-level AUROC and higher target-class F1 than the strongest prior model-level detector while using no greater optimization budget.

claim: A model-level backdoor audit of CLIP classifiers still works against an attacker who deliberately narrows the trigger so that only the exact pattern fires, and against backdoors planted in a fine-tuned image encoder instead of a prompt-tuning module. A backdoor counts as caught only when the model's anomaly score reaches 2 and the audit's recovered trigger achieves at least 50% attack success. Supported only if the audit catches a majority of the narrowed-trigger backdoors and every encoder-level backdoor tested.

provenance.title: CLIP-Inspector: Model-Level Backdoor Detection for Prompt-Tuned CLIP via OOD Trigger Inversion

_decision_rule: A backdoor counts as caught only when the model’s anomaly score is at least 2 and the audit’s candidate trigger achieves at least 50% attack success rate.

claim: Distances taken straight from frozen pretrained molecular encoders, which were never trained on any similarity objective, carry enough information about how alike two molecules are to serve two downstream jobs: ranking candidates in ligand-based virtual screening, and acting as the reward signal in reinforcement-learning molecule generation. Accepted only if at least one such representation reaches an absolute Pearson correlation of at least 0.50 with the corresponding established 3D similarity scores; reaches a best-pooled 1% enrichment factor above 2 on more than half of the screening targets with an average enrichment no lower than the strongest traditional similarity measure; and, in both a string-based and a synthesis-aware generator, produces candidates with higher mean predicted activity and higher sampling throughput than a reward based on 3D alignment.

provenance.title: Advancing Ligand-based Virtual Screening and Molecular Generation with Pretrained Molecular Embedding Distance

_decision_rule: The proposition is accepted only if at least one such representation attains an absolute Pearson correlation of at least 0.50 with corresponding established 3D similarity scores, achieves best-pooled EF1% greater than 2 on more than 50% of screening targets with average EF1% no lower than the strongest traditional similarity measure, and, in both string-based and synthesis-aware generation, yields candidates with higher mean predicted pIC50 and higher sampling throughput than a 3D-alignment reward.

claim: The usual bargain in adversarially trained image classifiers, where resistance to bounded perturbations is bought by giving up accuracy on untouched images, is not forced. A training objective can lift both at once instead of trading one against the other. Supported only if both clean accuracy and accuracy under attack rise by more than 0 percentage points against the conventional objective the method is built on, and only if both the plain average and the harmonic mean of the two exceed those of the strongest earlier approach trained under an equal budget by more than 0 points.

provenance.title: Robust Alignment: Harmonizing Clean Accuracy and Adversarial Robustness in Adversarial Training

_decision_rule: The claim is supported only if both clean accuracy and adversarial accuracy improve by more than 0 percentage points over the corresponding conventional adversarial-training objective, and if both their arithmetic mean and harmonic mean exceed those of the strongest prior adversarial-training approach under an equal training budget by more than 0 points.

claim: In adversarial training, resistance to attack is learned mainly from correctly classified training images that sit well away from the decision boundary, not from those hugging it. Call an image near-boundary if it can still be flipped at a tenth of the full perturbation budget, and far otherwise. Weakening the perturbation applied to near-boundary images should cost much less robustness than weakening it for far images. Supported only if, for weakening to a tenth of the budget and to zero, the robustness lost is smaller for near-boundary images than for far ones in both cases, full-strength perturbation of the far images beats both weakened variants on robust accuracy, and at least one way of drawing that near/far line raises clean and robust accuracy together relative to treating all correctly classified images the same.

provenance.title: Robust Alignment: Harmonizing Clean Accuracy and Adversarial Robustness in Adversarial Training

_decision_rule: The claim is supported only if, for reductions to one tenth of the full budget and to zero, each robust-accuracy loss is smaller for near-boundary samples than for far-from-boundary samples, full-strength perturbation of far-from-boundary samples exceeds both reduced-strength variants in robust accuracy by more than 0 percentage points, and at least one partition rule improves both clean and robust accuracy by more than 0 percentage points over treating all correctly classified samples alike.

claim: Vision-language-action manipulation policies inherit a real supply-chain weakness from their training pipeline: an adversary who can either taint a small share of the training data or fine-tune the released weights can plant a hidden visual condition that drives the robot to an attacker-chosen action. The question is whether such a thing survives in practice, meaning it fires on the condition while the policy still does its ordinary job, still fires when the instruction is reworded, and does not fire on innocuous scenes. Accepted only if, with no more than 5% of the training data tainted, the attacker-chosen action is produced in more than 80% of triggered trials while ordinary task success stays within 5% relative of a cleanly trained policy; if rewording the instruction, by synonym or by sentence structure, costs fewer than 5 percentage points of that figure; if innocuous scenes produce it under 8% of the time; and if, given fine-tuning access, it beats the strongest earlier attack on both the triggered figure and retained ordinary success at an equal access and training budget.

provenance.title: ATAAT: Adaptive Threat-Aware Adversarial Tuning Framework against Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models

_decision_rule: The claim is accepted if, with no more than 5% poisoned training data, targeted attack success exceeds 80% and benign task success remains within 5% relative of a clean-trained policy; synonym replacement or syntactic restructuring reduces targeted attack success by fewer than 5 percentage points; neutral-context activation remains below 8%; and, under direct fine-tuning access, the backdoor exceeds the strongest prior attack in both targeted attack success and retained benign task success under an equal access and training budget.

claim: Ordinary training-time visual backdoors fail to take hold in vision-language-action policies because the gradients for the ordinary task and for the hidden behaviour pull against each other during joint fine-tuning, and removing that opposition is what lets the hidden behaviour be learned without ruining ordinary performance. Accepted only if the conventional approach shows a training-averaged cosine similarity between the two gradient signals below 0 together with a failure to fit the action policy at all, while an approach built to remove the opposition keeps that similarity near zero, exceeds 80% on the triggered behaviour, and holds ordinary task success within 5% relative of a cleanly trained policy.

provenance.title: ATAAT: Adaptive Threat-Aware Adversarial Tuning Framework against Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models

_decision_rule: The claim is accepted if the conventional condition has training-averaged benign/backdoor gradient cosine similarity below 0, a condition designed to eliminate conflict has lower training-averaged absolute cosine similarity, targeted attack success above 80%, and benign task success within 5% relative of the unablated condition, while removing either required property lowers targeted attack success below 5% and keeps benign task success within 5% relative of the unablated condition.

claim: The defences available for this setting, meaning input preprocessing, parameter pruning, runtime safety layers, and backdoor detectors carried over from classification to continuous control, cannot be relied on to remove a semantically triggered backdoor from a vision-language-action policy without raising too many false alarms on ordinary inputs. Accepted only if no defence cuts the triggered behaviour by at least 50 percentage points relative to the undefended policy while keeping false alarms on benign inputs at or below 10%; a defence that reaches the first bar only by exceeding the second does not count.

provenance.title: ATAAT: Adaptive Threat-Aware Adversarial Tuning Framework against Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models

_decision_rule: The claim is accepted if no defense lowers targeted attack success by at least 50 percentage points relative to the undefended policy while keeping the false-positive rate on benign inputs at or below 10%; a defense that meets the attack-reduction threshold only above that false-positive ceiling does not count as reliable.

claim: Methods that write new knowledge into a large language model by changing its weights are a workable option for instruction-following and reasoning models, both for single facts and for complex events, and both for one update and for many applied in sequence. Workable means that, at the same editing workload, the average over edit reliability, generalisation, locality and portability is at least as high as the strongest alternative that stores the update outside the model, while accuracy on unrelated general and reasoning tasks stays at 100% or more of what the model scored before editing, that is no relative degradation at all. Both the single-update and the sequential setting have to hold, not just isolated updates.

provenance.title: Revisiting Parameter-Based Knowledge Editing in Large Language Models

_decision_rule: They count as viable only if, at the same editing workload, their arithmetic mean across edit reliability, generalization, locality, and portability is at least as high as that of the strongest external-memory alternative, while accuracy on unrelated general and reasoning tasks remains at least 100% of the model’s pre-edit accuracy, corresponding to 0% relative degradation.

claim: A weight edit aimed at one fact spreads disproportionately into the directions of the model's representation space that carry the least variance, and the size of that spreading predicts how fast editing quality decays as edits accumulate. Spreading in a direction means a change that is large compared with that direction's own scale before editing. Supported only if the most affected directions sit among the lowest-variance ones, if a single edit already exceeds the native scale of some directions, and if the amount of spreading correlates negatively, at p below 0.05, with at least three of reliability, generalisation, locality and portability, for at least half of the weight-editing methods examined.

provenance.title: Revisiting Parameter-Based Knowledge Editing in Large Language Models

_decision_rule: The proposition is supported only if directions in the lower half of the nonzero singular-value spectrum have both a larger median R_k and a larger fraction of directions with R_k ≥ 1 than the upper half, and amplification has a negative Spearman correlation at p < 0.05 with at least three of reliability, generalization, locality, and portability for at least half of the parameter-editing approaches tested.

claim: Learning circuits over a language model's components, both raw neurons and the much larger set of features produced by a sparse autoencoder, can be made cheaper to compute without losing structural accuracy or practical usefulness. Counted as successful if its error in recovering the circuit's dependency structure is statistically indistinguishable at the 0.05 level from the strongest earlier intervention-based approach while taking less wall-clock time; if the resulting feature circuit is no less faithful and no more complete than that approach; and if using the circuit to guide a domain-generalisation task matches or beats the strongest alternative that does not peek at the answer, again in less time. Structural recovery here means getting the dependency skeleton right, not estimating exact causal edge weights.

provenance.title: Scalable Circuit Learning for Interpreting Large Language Models

_decision_rule: It is considered successful if its structural-recovery error differs nonsignificantly at the 0.05 level from the strongest prior intervention-based approach while requiring less wall-clock runtime, its feature-circuit faithfulness is no lower and completeness no higher than that approach, and circuit-guided domain generalization matches or exceeds the strongest non-oracle alternative in prediction accuracy while requiring less runtime.

claim: Language-model agents can be useful explainers of transformer circuits that have already been located for them, both by saying what each component does and by saying what the circuit computes as a whole. Useful means at least one agent classifies more than half of the components correctly, scores above 0.50 on a 0-to-1 scale for the quality of its written role descriptions, where 0, 0.5 and 1 stand for wrong, partly right and right, and names the overall task correctly for more than half the circuits. Because the circuit is handed over in advance, this is about explanation after localisation, not about finding circuits.

provenance.title: Can Language Model Agents be Helpful Circuit Explainers in Mechanistic Interpretability?

_decision_rule: Helpfulness is established if at least one agent correctly classifies more than 50% of circuit components, achieves mean role-description quality above 0.50 on a 0–1 scale where 0, 0.5, and 1 represent incorrect, partially correct, and correct descriptions, and correctly identifies the overall task for more than 50% of circuits.

claim: For agents explaining circuits that have already been located, imposing a staged workflow of observe, hypothesise, then test causally produces better explanations than either cutting a stage out of that workflow or letting an equally capable agent work however it likes with the same tools. Counts as better than the cut-down versions only if it gives strictly higher circuit-level task accuracy for every model when each stage is removed in turn, and wins more than half the resulting component-level comparisons. Counts as better than unrestricted tool use only if both component classification and role-description quality are strictly higher while circuit-level task accuracy is no lower.

provenance.title: Can Language Model Agents be Helpful Circuit Explainers in Mechanistic Interpretability?

_decision_rule: The workflow counts as better than incomplete variants only if it achieves strictly higher circuit-level task-description accuracy for every evaluated model when each key stage is removed in turn and wins more than 50% of the resulting component-role tagging and role-description-quality comparisons; it counts as better than unrestricted tool use only if both component-role tagging accuracy and role-description quality are strictly higher while circuit-level task-description accuracy is no lower.

claim: When these agents fail at explaining a located circuit, the failure sits in testing the hypothesis rather than in forming it. Hypotheses count as mostly grounded in what the agent observed if their mean human grounding score is above 1 on a 0-to-2 scale, where 0 is unsupported, 1 partly supported and 2 fully supported. Testing is the bottleneck if the plans for testing average below both that grounding score and the fully sound score of 2, if code written to run those tests fails some of the time, and if components are still unresolved once the iteration budget runs out. The attribution additionally requires that the agent with the fewest unresolved components also has the highest final component accuracy, and the one with the most has the lowest final scores.

provenance.title: Can Language Model Agents be Helpful Circuit Explainers in Mechanistic Interpretability?

_decision_rule: Validation is the bottleneck if validation plans average below both the grounding score and the fully sound score of 2, code-execution success is below 100%, and components remain unresolved after three hypothesis-validation iterations.

claim: In two aligned chat models, a jailbreak that succeeds does not wipe out the model's internal representation of harm; it routes around it. Components that carry the refusal decision are knocked down, while other safety-relevant attention heads stay active even on the attacks that work. A safety-relevant head counts as attack-resistant if its activation distributions for refused harmful requests and for successful attacks overlap by at least 0.5, and as compromised if that overlap is below 0.5 and its standardised activation falls under attack. Knocking down a small set of heads counts as a sufficient local route to bypassing refusal if suppressing at most eight of them lifts attack success from roughly 0% to at least 80%, with non-overlapping 95% intervals against suppressing the same number of heads chosen at random. The surviving representation has practical value if, with no extra training, reading it classifies harmful inputs better than the model's own refusal behaviour and matches or beats the strongest purpose-built safety classifier on aggregate Macro-F1.

provenance.title: Robust Harmful Features Under Jailbreak Attacks

_decision_rule: Selective suppression constitutes a localized sufficient pathway for refusal bypass if suppressing at most eight safety-relevant heads raises attack success from approximately 0% to at least 80% and exceeds equal-sized random-head interventions with nonoverlapping 95% confidence intervals.

claim: The safety signal that survives a successful jailbreak in these models is held up in part by a distinct population of middle-layer attention heads, and the heads that get knocked down are knocked down by the tokens of the jailbreak wrapper rather than by the harmful request inside it. Supported only if suppressing the surviving heads during successful attacks cuts mean absolute middle-layer safety activation by at least 10% against leaving them alone, and if, when each head's activation is attributed back to input tokens, the tokens of the harmful request push both populations the same way while the wrapper tokens push them in opposite directions.

provenance.title: Robust Harmful Features Under Jailbreak Attacks

_decision_rule: The proposition is supported only if suppressing the persistent heads during successful jailbreaks reduces mean absolute mid-layer safety activation by at least 10% relative to leaving those heads intact, the two head populations’ median standardized contributions from harmful-request tokens differ by no more than 0.15, and their template-token medians lie on opposite sides of zero and are separated by more than three standard deviations.

claim: Plane-geometry problems written only in prose can be turned automatically into theorem statements in a standard proof assistant and its mainline mathematics library, in a way that keeps the meaning and that general-purpose neural provers can work with. Keeping the meaning requires the formal statement, including whatever non-degeneracy and configuration assumptions have to be spelled out, to say what the prose said. Supported if expert review finds the first compiling candidate correct for at least half of the problems, or a correct candidate among five attempts for at least half; if a general-purpose prover given no geometry-specific training proves more than 0% of them on a single attempt; and if training on the resulting statements raises that figure by more than 0 percentage points over the same starting checkpoint.

provenance.title: Euclean: Automated Geometry Problem Formalization with Unified Verification in Lean

_decision_rule: The proposition is supported if expert review finds a correct first compiling candidate for at least 50% of problems or a correct candidate among five attempts for at least 50%, an unadapted general-purpose prover achieves greater than 0% single-attempt proof success, and training on the formalizations improves that success rate by more than 0 percentage points over the same unadapted checkpoint.

claim: Training a general-purpose theorem prover on automatically formalised geometry produces a gain that is not confined to the data it was trained on nor to the one prover used to collect that data. The question is whether the gain survives on held-out competition problems never used in training and reappears when a second, independently pretrained prover is given the same treatment. Supported only if proof success exceeds the matching untrained checkpoint by more than 0 percentage points both on the held-out problems and for the second prover.

provenance.title: Euclean: Automated Geometry Problem Formalization with Unified Verification in Lean

_decision_rule: The proposition is supported only if proof success exceeds the corresponding unadapted checkpoint by more than 0 percentage points both on the held-out competition problems and for the second prover after geometry-specific training.

claim: Multimodal language models built by adapting a text backbone pick up sparse internal features that causally and selectively govern particular behaviours: reasoning about spatial relations, reading text that appears in an image, and unsafe responses conditioned on what the image shows. If so, those features should also be better handles for steering than generic internal directions. Accepted only if removing a target feature lowers its associated spatial or text-reading accuracy, or lowers the success rate of attacks that exploit unsafe image-conditioned behaviour, by more than 0 percentage points beyond both the change in general visual question answering and the change on a matched non-target control, while also beating matched random-feature removal and removal of features picked without regard to the multimodal adaptation. Steering aimed at those features must additionally raise average target-task accuracy by more than 0 percentage points over equally strong steering that does not use behaviour-linked sparse features.

provenance.title: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control

_decision_rule: The claim is accepted only if removing a target feature lowers its associated spatial or image-text-reading accuracy, or lowers unsafe-behavior attack success, by an absolute margin greater than 0 percentage points over both the change in general visual-question-answering performance and the change on a matched non-target control, while also exceeding matched random-feature removal and removal of features chosen without regard to multimodal adaptation; interventions targeted to those features must additionally improve average target-task accuracy by more than 0 percentage points over equally strong interventions that do not use behavior-linked sparse features.

claim: A general-purpose robotic manipulation system can pick up flat objects of varied shape and material, both rigid and deformable, and keep working on objects and whole categories it never trained on. The generalisation has to cover two things at once: unfamiliar instances of familiar categories, and objects from categories never seen at all. Supported only if mean grasp success strictly exceeds that of the strongest earlier approach under matched evaluation conditions in each of the three regimes, training objects, unseen objects from trained categories, and objects from unseen categories, counting a trial successful only when the object stays aloft without slipping for at least two seconds after the final action.

provenance.title: FlatLab: A Unified Methodology Framework and Simulation-Based Benchmark for Robotic Manipulation of Flat Objects

_decision_rule: The claim is supported only if the system’s average grasp-success rate strictly exceeds that of the strongest prior approach under matched evaluation conditions in each of three regimes—training objects, unseen objects from trained categories, and objects from unseen categories—with a trial counted as successful only when the object remains aloft without slipping for at least two seconds after the final action.

claim: When a language model is trained by reinforcement learning to obey several instructions inside a single response, its exploration drifts toward the instructions it already finds easy, and that drift is what holds the training back. Supported only if a policy trained to counteract the drift ends with lower spread in per-instruction success and lower variance in how often pairs of instructions are satisfied together, each by more than 0 absolute units, than an otherwise identical equal-reward policy, while its mean share of prompts where every instruction passes is higher by more than 0 percentage points. Separately, each of those two imbalance measures counts as a valid diagnostic only if, holding mean per-instruction accuracy fixed, it correlates negatively with the share of prompts where every instruction passes.

provenance.title: Mitigating Exploration Bias in RL for Multi-Instruction Following

_decision_rule: The claim is supported only if a policy trained to counteract this bias has variation in per-instruction success and variance in pairwise co-satisfaction each lower by more than 0 absolute units than an otherwise matched equal-reward RL policy, while its mean prompt-level all-instructions-pass accuracy is higher by more than 0 percentage points.

claim: A vision-language-action manipulation policy can adapt at test time to task families left out of its adaptation training, using expert demonstrations supplied as context rather than any weight update. What is at stake is both how well it executes the novel task and how its inference cost scales, in simulation and on real hardware. Accepted only if mean whole-task success exceeds that of the strongest earlier in-context imitation policy, under equal training and equal expert-context budgets, in both settings, while the growth in inference latency per additional expert segment is lower than that policy's growth.

provenance.title: RA-VLA: Retrieval-Augmented VLA for Test-Time Adaptation

_decision_rule: The claim is accepted only if mean whole-task success exceeds that of the strongest prior in-context imitation policy under equal training and expert-context budgets in both settings, while inference-latency growth per additional expert segment is lower than that strongest prior policy’s growth.

claim: Existing in-context imitation policies for these models adapt poorly for two specific reasons: their retrieval picks context that looks similar rather than context that behaves similarly, and their action predictions barely depend on the retrieved context at all. Dependence is measured as the size of the change in generated actions when relevant context is swapped for random context, relative to the size of the action generated with relevant context, read together with held-out whole-task success. Accepted only if, holding the policy fixed, behaviour-matched retrieval both returns a higher share of cross-demonstration neighbours from the corresponding phase of the motion and yields higher held-out success than appearance-based retrieval, and if existing policies show both lower context dependence and lower held-out success than a comparable policy built to attend to its context.

provenance.title: RA-VLA: Retrieval-Augmented VLA for Test-Time Adaptation

_decision_rule: The claim is accepted only if behaviorally matched retrieval yields both a higher fraction of cross-demonstration nearest-neighbor segments from corresponding motion phases and higher held-out whole-task success than generic visual-similarity retrieval under an otherwise fixed policy, while existing policies have both lower Relative Contextual Sensitivity and lower held-out success than an otherwise comparable context-grounded policy.

claim: A vision-language-action manipulation policy can be made to recover on its own from two different kinds of trouble: arm poses that drift away from anything it was trained on while the scene itself is still workable, and failures that leave the scene in a state the task never passes through. The deciding bar is a strictly higher mean end-to-end task success rate than both the strongest earlier comparison system and the same policy without recovery training, together with a strictly higher success rate than that unmodified policy on every physical-robot task evaluated. Recovery has to happen without a human supplying correction during deployment, and has to leave the policy able to resume and finish the original task.

provenance.title: FLARE: A Failure-Aware Framework for Autonomous Correction and Recovery in Visual-Language Robotic Manipulation

_decision_rule: The decisive bar is a strictly higher mean end-to-end task success rate than the strongest prior comparison system and the same VLA without failure-recovery training, together with a strictly higher success rate than that unmodified VLA on every evaluated physical-robot task.

claim: Decoding an instruction-tuned language model under a context-free grammar, within a finite token budget, can guarantee that what comes back is actually accepted by the grammar, rather than only guaranteeing that each prefix could in principle still be completed, and can improve the quality of the structures produced at the same time. The validity bar is that 100% of returned outputs are accepted by the target grammar, with nothing invalid or truncated returned whenever an accepted completion can be certified inside the available budget. The quality bar is that task-specific correctness exceeds that of the strongest applicable earlier constrained decoder, using the same base model and the same token budget.

provenance.title: Stay Within Your Bounds: Distance-Guided Decoding for Guaranteed Context-Free Grammar Compliance

_decision_rule: The validity bar is that 100% of returned outputs are accepted by the target grammar, with no invalid or truncated output returned when an accepted completion is certified within the available token budget.

claim: A multimodal-language-model agent for continuous vision-language navigation can get around unseen environments efficiently using nothing but a single forward-facing colour camera, ordinary offline expert supervision, and no auxiliary spatial model. Supported only if it beats the strongest earlier agent working under the same resource constraints on both success rate and success weighted by path efficiency in unseen environments, while staying under 24 GB of peak inference memory and running with lower per-step latency than that comparator. It fails if the advantage needs extra training data, richer sensors, external spatial tools, or more memory than that.

provenance.title: LookStep: Efficient Vision-Language Navigation with Linguistic Foresight and Event Driven Memory

_decision_rule: The proposition is supported only if such an agent exceeds the strongest prior agent subject to the same resource constraints in both unseen-environment success rate and success-weighted path efficiency, while using no more than 24 GB of peak inference memory and lower per-step inference latency than that comparator.

claim: A navigation agent trained only on the standard continuous-navigation datasets carries over to a different navigation task and dataset, and to a physical robot in a workspace it has never seen, without any real-world fine-tuning. Supported only if it exceeds the strongest earlier system under the same transfer conditions on both success rate and path-weighted success, and succeeds in more than half of physical-robot trials, counting a trial successful only when the robot stops within one metre of the instructed target.

provenance.title: LookStep: Efficient Vision-Language Navigation with Linguistic Foresight and Event Driven Memory

_decision_rule: The proposition is supported only if the agent exceeds the strongest prior system under the same transfer conditions in both success rate and success-weighted path efficiency, and succeeds in more than 50% of physical-robot trials, with a trial counted as successful only when the robot stops within 1 meter of the instructed target.

claim: One deployable humanoid control policy, driven by high-level skill commands, can carry out several different ball-interaction skills, switch between them on command, and complete long sequences of them after being transferred from simulation to a real robot. Supported only if, under an equal training budget, its full-sequence success rate is strictly higher than that of the strongest earlier single-stage multi-skill controller at both evaluated sequence lengths, and its success rate on the physical robot is strictly higher than a matched conventional motion-prior controller on every atomic and composite task evaluated. Full-sequence success means completing every commanded subskill in order, not merely reaching some intermediate stage.

provenance.title: SkillX: Unified Multi-Skill Policy Learning for Humanoid Soccer

_decision_rule: The claim is supported only if, under an equal training budget, the policy’s full-sequence success rate is strictly higher than that of the strongest prior single-stage multi-skill controller at both evaluated composition horizons, and its physical-robot success rate is strictly higher than a matched conventional motion-prior controller on every evaluated atomic and composite task.

claim: Embodied task planners driven by a vision-language model, working from a single first-person view, can stay aware of hazards they met earlier after those hazards are hidden or pass out of view. Supported only if a planner that keeps prior safety-relevant information about the environment achieves a higher safe-success rate than both the strongest earlier safety-aware planner and an otherwise identical planner that sees only the current observation, using the same underlying model, while reaching an ordinary task-success rate at least as high as an unmodified planner, in both simulation and physical execution. Safe success means finishing the assigned task while also meeting its safety goal.

claim: Staying aware of hidden hazards requires remembering the relationships among objects seen earlier, not merely retaining past observations or a list of what was seen. Supported only if relationship-preserving memory gives a higher safe-success rate than each of full visual history, retrieved textual descriptions of earlier observations, and a relationship-free list of seen objects, and also beats otherwise matched memories that drop objects once they leave view or that fail to revise remembered relationships after actions that change them.
